# api

`github.com/lnorton89/golc/internal/api`

Package api implements CONTEXT Phase 7's first working vertical slice
of the versioned external control API: a Chi+Huma HTTP server, mounted
under the "/v1" path prefix (D-02), hosted inside the existing Art-Net
daemon process (D-07) as one more ordered Subsystem.

Every handler is a thin translator (07-RESEARCH.md Pattern 1): it turns
an HTTP request into a synthetic routed invocation and calls Execute on
the injected Executor, then turns the outcome back into an HTTP
response (translate.go's translateResult). This package never reaches
a domain package (pool/scene/show/...) directly, and it never imports
the CLI command-execution package that owns the real registry --
package Executor is the whole point of the seam: the daemon-side
command-execution package constructs a small adapter satisfying this
interface and injects it via NewServer, so this package depends only on
a three-method contract, never on the execution package's import path.
(See 07-RESEARCH.md's "Architecture Patterns" and this repo's own
artnet daemon doc comment for why: the execution package already
imports the Art-Net daemon package, and the Art-Net daemon package must
never import this one either -- an api->execution import here would
close a three-package cycle. internal/routecatalog is a test-only
bridge that exists solely so this package's own tests can reach a real
registry without this package's production code ever doing so.)

server.go's *Server satisfies the Art-Net daemon's Subsystem shape
(Start(ctx) error; Shutdown(ctx) error) structurally -- no import of
the daemon package is needed for that either.

translate.go injects the daemon's own fixed show path into every
show-domain routed call server-side; no request ever carries a
client-supplied path (07-RESEARCH.md Pitfall 3, T-07-02).

This plan (07-02) intentionally ships only a handful of read routes
(GET /v1/config/{concern}, GET /v1/show) plus the capability-coverage
gate that makes API-01's "every public capability" claim mechanically
checkable as later plans add auth, mutations, dry-run, batch, and SSE.
